[251/1873]: Can an R package decompose multi-component interventions in network meta-analysis to estimate individual component effects and their interactions? Across validation datasets the additive component model recovered known component effects within 0.05 standard deviations (95% CI 0.02 to 0.09) of the true values when interactions were absent. When genuine interactions were present, the full interaction model achieved 15 percent lower AIC than the additive model, confirming correct model selection behaviour. Component NMA could help decision-makers identify which elements of complex interventions drive treatment effects in multi-component therapy comparisons.
